text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING AND MARKETING:

PARIS - Advertising agency Publicis says it has settled a year-long dispute with former U.S. ally True North and will develop a global network of agencies under its own name. It will transfer to True North the FCB agencies in Paris, London, Lisbon and Athens. Both companies will withdraw their respective legal claims against each other. True North says it will form a new European network by uniting four FCB offics it and Publicis formerly ran with Wilkens Internationa.
LONDON - Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising says it is merging a small London sister agency, K Advertising, into its global network. Both are owned by Cordiant Plc.

LONDON - Bartle Bogle Hegarty says it will not re-pitch for the European advertising account of Haagen-Dazs, for which it created ads emphasising the ice cream's sensual pleasures. Industry sources say BBH felt it merited better treatment by the ice cream brand's parent company, Pillsbury Europe.

WASHINGTON - National Association of Securities Dealers says it will launch an unprecedented broadcast media campaign to educate the public on how to be smarter investors. The initiative is the "first coast-to-coast public service announcement television and radio campaign ever undertaken" by a securities market regulator, NASD says.

GENEVA - Swiss watchmaker Swatch's advertisement hailing Swiss skiing champions for bringing home gold medals. sparks a debate about good taste among ad industry executives who say it could offend Jews in the wake of the Nazi gold issue. "As always, whenever there is gold, a good part of it ends up in Switzerland," says the ad.
MEDIA AND THE INTERNET:
PARIS - The French Senate debates a bill to reform public broadcasting, to give a legal framework to satellite television and provide a new framework for radio.
MILAN - Italian private broadcaster Mediaset, part of Silvio Berlusconi's media empire, says it will invest 240 billion lire ($142.9 million) in Italian and European screen products in 1997.

VIENNA - Austria, one of the last strongholds of state-controlled broadcasting, unveiled a draft law that will open the market to private radio and television stations and break the monopoly of state-owned ORF.
GENEVA - A Swiss company hopes to redefine private banking with a modem and the click of a mouse by offering asset management services to clients via Internet-type technology.

NEW YORK - U S West Inc says it has no plans to buy more cable television properties, although it may under some circumstances trade properties to improve its portfolio."We've pretty much got enough on our plate," says Richard McCormick, Chief Executive of U S West Inc.

NEW YORK - A new editor has taken over from the legendary Helen Gurley Brown at Cosmopolitan Magazine, but readers need not fear: the orgasm articles are bigger and better than ever. The first issue edited by Brown's successor, Bonnie Fuller, features a cover bearing the words "His and Her orgasms" in big, black, bold type.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS AND MARKETS:

BRUSSELS - Alliances rather than straight takeovers will play a rising part in the future of the retail sector as it copes with increasing globalisation, leading Belgian retailer Delhaize, says. Retailers will need to switch their focus to the developing countries of Asia and Latin America as other economies slow down.

TEL AVIV - Unilever PLC has set its sights on serving the local market in its 18-month-old drive to establish a major presence in Israel, the company's Israel chairman Ray Bremner says. If Unilever does decide to use its Israeli operations to serve foreign markets, they will be in Europe and the United States -- not the Middle East, he says.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. - Fresh Choice Inc says it expects to post a loss in the first quarter due to heavy spending on advertising. The company says it has launched an aggressive marketing campaign to help boost sales. Fresh Choice is promoting itself on television for the first time, on radio and in print.

WASHINGTON - Commerce Secretary William Daley says that U.S. exports to China rose a modest two percent last year and that Washington must continue to press China to open its markets to more U.S. goods. "China's market remains far too closed to our exports," he says.

TOKYO - Canon Inc, manufacturer of cameras, printers and photocopiers, says it has earned record profits in 1996, benefiting from the global boom in personal computers. The company expects the good news to continue this year, "Computer peripherals such as bubble-jet printers and laser printers will remain brisk, helping push up sales," a Canon director says.
SANTIAGO - A group of investors including The Coca Cola Company is in talks to buy five percent of Chilean bottler Embotelladora Andina for around $100 million, newspapers report.

TOKYO - The Japanese car industry says it will continue to boost exchanges with its Chinese counterpart. A trade body representing Japanese car manufacturers says the industry is to pursue a closer relationship with the Chinese auto industry.
NEW YORK - Compaq Computer Corp plans to announce that it will sell a personal computer priced at less than $1,000, according to a newspaper report.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

BRUSSELS - Luxury chocolate company Neuhaus, exports to 36 countries around the globe and has its sights set on more. "We want to be number one on the Belgian market for luxury chocolates and see good prospects for growth in other countries," chief executive officer Marlene Vonken says.

NAPLES, Fla. - General Mills Inc says it expects a recovery in sales volume in the $9.0 billion U.S. ready-to-eat cereal market, in which it is the number two player. To combat sluggish cereal sales, U.S. cereal makers have cut prices and stepped up new product launches.
